question: Aspirin is contraindicated as an antipyretic in children with dengue or chickenpox because it is associated with Reye syndrome and increased bleeding risk.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Aspirin must never be given to febrile children with dengue or chickenpox. In dengue, aspirin inhibits platelet function and worsens bleeding. In chickenpox and influenza, aspirin is associated with Reye syndrome. Always use paracetamol for fever management in these conditions.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Aspirin is absolutely contraindicated in children with dengue (inhibits platelet function, worsening thrombocytopaenia and bleeding risk) and in chickenpox/influenza (associated with Reye syndrome — a rare but potentially fatal hepatic and cerebral disorder). Paracetamol is the antipyretic of choice in these conditions.
